extracted.subtask_description: Practical how-to guidance for early-career researchers on composing journal peer reviews, covering structure, tone, procedural norms, and reviewer behaviours. Focused on producing useful, constructive reviews for ecology/biology manuscripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary (1–3 sentences)
rubrics_metrics.description: Overview of the paper's main argument, quality assessment, and key shortcomings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep this section concise (1–3 sentences) and state the central claim, your overall assessment, and the most important problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantial problems with design, interpretation, analysis, argumentation, writing — and praise where merited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on big-picture flaws that affect validity or interpretation; include praise when deserved to balance critique and clarify strengths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minor remarks
rubrics_metrics.description: Typos, citation errors, non-fatal issues, often as bullets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List small, fixable items (formatting, minor clarifications, editorial fixes) typically in bullet form for easy actioning by authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read the journal's reviewer instructions first
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the specific journal's guidance before writing — follow their requested structure, confidential comments, or scoring scheme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Find something genuinely praiseworthy
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify at least one real strength even in a poor paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pointing out strengths helps authors and sets a constructive tone; avoid token praise that isn't sincere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact the editor with questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct procedural or ethical questions to the editor — that's their job.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unsure about scope, confidentiality, or handling sensitive issues, ask the editor rather than making assumptions in the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond promptly to invitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Click 'no' immediately if you can't commit to reviewing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely responses help editors secure reviewers and reduce delays; don't accept if you cannot meet deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: When declining, suggest alternative reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommend other qualified reviewers when you decline, especially doctoral candidates and postdocs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offering alternatives (including early-career researchers) is helpful to editors and supports community review capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address the editor, not the authors directly
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should be written to the editor unless the journal requests otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep formulation and recommendations directed at the editor; use the appropriate confidential or public review sections as instructed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid prescriptive language; explain problems and why solutions work
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not issue orders; explain the problem and why a proposed solution would help.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer explanatory phrasing over commands so authors understand reasoning and can choose appropriate fixes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be culturally sensitive about writing quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Be mindful when commenting on language, especially for non-native English speakers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on clarity and scientific content rather than critiquing language in a way that could be culturally insensitive; offer constructive, specific suggestions for improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polite language while staying honest about shortcomings
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain politeness but be frank about substantive problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance courtesy with clear identification of flaws; politeness does not mean avoiding necessary criticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phrase suggestions gently in main reviews; reserve unvarnished assessment for editor-only sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Use milder wording in the version authors see; give candid judgments to editors in confidential comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you need to be blunt about suitability for publication or ethical concerns, use the editor-only section rather than the author-facing review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't pile on about poor writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid extensive commentary solely about bad prose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make a few carefully chosen remarks about writing; focus effort on substantive scientific issues instead of repeatedly criticizing style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skip detailed reviews if comprehension is genuinely impossible; tell the editor
rubrics_metrics.description: If the manuscript cannot be understood, do not attempt a detailed review — inform the editor instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain to the editor that comprehension was impossible and why, rather than producing low-value line edits or guesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide constructive, specific feedback (community service)
rubrics_metrics.description: Give actionable, concrete criticism; this is community service, especially valuable for authors with limited peer-review access before submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be specific about what to change and why; targeted suggestions are more useful than vague negative statements.
